  "cut_point": "We are given:

- The **length of the train** = 300 meters
- The **time to pass through the tunnel** (from front to back) = 1 minute = 60 seconds
- The **time the train is completely inside the tunnel** = 30 seconds

We are to find the **length of the tunnel**.

---

### Step 1: Understand the scenario

When the **front of the train enters the tunnel**, the **back of the train is still outside**. As the train moves forward, the **back of the train exits the tunnel** when the **front of the train has traveled the full length of the tunnel plus the length of the train**.

So, the total distance the train travels to completely pass through the tunnel is:

$$
\text{Distance} = \text{Length of tunnel} + \text{Length of train}
$$

This distance is covered in **60 seconds**.

---

### Step 2: Find the speed of the train

$$
\text{Speed} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}} = \frac{\text{Length of tunnel} + 300}{60}
$$

---

### Step 3: When is the train completely inside the tunnel?

The time when the **train is completely inside the tunnel** is **30 seconds**.",

      "For the entire train to pass through, the front travels the tunnel length plus the train length, so speed v = (L + 300)/60.",

    "error_reason": "This misinterprets the given 30 seconds as the instant when the train first becomes fully inside. It is actually the duration for which the whole train remains completely inside the tunnel, from the moment the rear enters until the front reaches the exit.",

  }

annotation.cut_point:
We are given:

- The **length of the train** = 300 meters
- The **time to pass through the tunnel** (from front to back) = 1 minute = 60 seconds
- The **time the train is completely inside the tunnel** = 30 seconds

We are to find the **length of the tunnel**.

---

### Step 1: Understand the scenario

When the **front of the train enters the tunnel**, the **back of the train is still outside**. As the train moves forward, the **back of the train exits the tunnel** when the **front of the train has traveled the full length of the tunnel plus the length of the train**.

So, the total distance the train travels to completely pass through the tunnel is:

$$
\text{Distance} = \text{Length of tunnel} + \text{Length of train}
$$

This distance is covered in **60 seconds**.

---

### Step 2: Find the speed of the train

$$
\text{Speed} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}} = \frac{\text{Length of tunnel} + 300}{60}
$$

---

### Step 3: When is the train completely inside the tunnel?

The time when the **train is completely inside the tunnel** is **30 seconds**.
